swap.evidence: Products: a vet clinic's appointment booking; a council allotment waiting list. Survives unchanged: masthead (small outline icon + bold wordmark + three text links), pale green-grey ground, white bordered 4px cards with a square icon tile, single dark-green filled button, one sans, month calendar of white boxes, radio-card list. Bound to this product: tool names and specs, deposits, 'Available from' dates, 'Open' session markers, volunteer/desk copy. With the name hidden, a reader would know it is a tool library only from the copy, not from any visual element (the wrench glyph is the sole visual hint and is used as a filler).

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a community/charity booking flow: pale or white ground, one muted green 'community' accent, bordered cards, a friendly geometric sans, outline icons, a calendar picker. Predicted opposite: a bold hand-made, workshop-poster or pegboard look. The render matches the default on every identity-carrying element (ground, accent, type voice, card frame, icon tiles); nothing matches the opposite, and nothing departs from the default.

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'online booking for a neighbourhood repair cafe's drop-in slots, mostly phone users'. Predicted: white/pale masthead, green CTA, card list with icon thumbnails, calendar with available days marked, radio list of slots, check-and-confirm page. Overlap is near total, including the first viewport of every page; only copy differs.

Product-specific material is the copy and content (tool names, deposits, 'Open' session days, membership card), which is good but carried by a portable frame: rubric anchor 1.

attributes.x_evidence: Concrete specs (13 mm keyless chuck, 1.7 kg with battery), deposit on every card, 'Nothing is paid online. Bring the deposit and your membership card', one filled button per page, sticky reserve bar within thumb reach.
attributes.y_evidence: Nothing glossy or marketing-like; the neutral card frame is closer to a generic service template than to corporate, but does not pull toward Y.

attributes.x_evidence: Copy only: 'Fernhill Tool Library is run by volunteers. Questions: call the desk on 01632 960552', 'A volunteer will check the tool with you', 'Enough for a day of fixing shelves and a fence'.
attributes.y_evidence: Nothing folksy. But no visual lever expresses neighbourly: no photo of the room or the tools, no local mark, the green of the membership card is claimed in DESIGN.md but the card itself never appears.

attributes.x_evidence: Consistent borders and radius, accessible error summary at 375, dates in the declared format, deposit restated on confirm and done.
attributes.y_evidence: Care lapses rather than fuss: two label-column widths in the tool details table, truncated names at 375, sessions listed latest-first, cramped session cards at 1280, 'Basket (1)' after confirmation, dark-mode badge chip inconsistency.

brand_fit.weakest_pair: neighbourly, not folksy: carried by copy alone; the visuals are neutral and could belong to any service

mode_fit: All surfaces are Operate (done is Read). Quiet, conventional structure is correct and there is no hero moment or choreography, which fits. The gap is not too little expression for the mode but a missing identity floor: Operate surfaces still carry type, colour roles and real content, and here the one imagery slot is a filler glyph.

detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: Detectors reported zero hits. Nothing in the detector output changes the verdicts. Possible SLP-28 (emerald sole accent): #1f5a3a is near the band, but DESIGN.md gives a reason (the membership card's green), so it would be a false positive here had it fired.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench glyph as its thumbnail
findings.description: All ten cards on the find page use an identical wrench outline in a pale green square where a tool image would go. The slot reads as a placeholder, adds no information to tell a ladder from a pressure washer, and is the largest graphic element on the page. For members scanning for 'the drill with two batteries' on a phone, a picture or a tool-specific glyph would carry recognition; the repeated filler makes the page look unfinished.
findings.impact: May slow visual scanning and makes the catalogue look like a template awaiting content.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the thumbnail slot is for: real photographs of the library's own tools, a per-category glyph set, or remove the slot so the name and availability lead.

findings.title: No signature or identity beyond the name in bold text
findings.description: Across find, tool, basket, confirm and done, the only identity is 'Fernhill Tool Library' set in bold body type beside a small icon. Ground, accent, type and card frame match the category default and fail the swap, category-guess and similar-prompt tests. The product's own world (the community-centre room, the membership card whose green is cited in DESIGN.md, the session rhythm of Saturday mornings and Wednesday evenings) is absent from the visuals.
findings.impact: The service is likely to feel interchangeable with any booking form, weakening the 'neighbourly' attribute the brief asks for.
findings.recommendation: Choose one signature from the library's own mechanism (for example the session rhythm, already present as 'Open' tags) and carry it quietly across pages; let the masthead be a designed mark rather than body text.

findings.title: Tool names truncate with ellipsis at 375, making the two drills identical
findings.description: At 375 px card titles are cut to one line: both drills show 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...', and 'Extension ladder 3 m ...', 'Pressure washer, 130 ...' lose the distinguishing spec. The distinguishing detail is exactly what members use ('the drill with two batteries'). Phones are the main device.
findings.impact: May lead members to open the wrong drill or open both to compare.
findings.recommendation: Let titles wrap on narrow widths, or give the title the full card width above the thumbnail.

findings.title: Search field moves below all ten cards on phones
findings.description: At 1280 the search field sits above the grid; at 375 it appears after the tenth card, just above 'Opening times'. The page's job is 'find a tool', and on the main device the finding control is demoted below ~2,000 px of cards.
findings.impact: Members with a specific tool in mind may not see search without scrolling the whole list.
findings.recommendation: Keep the source order of search before results at every width.

findings.title: Basket session cards: latest-first order and one oversized card above five cramped ones
findings.description: At 1280 the six sessions are listed from Wed 28 Oct back to Sat 10 Oct. The first card spans the whole row; the remaining five share a row and wrap to three lines each. The layout gives most weight to the least likely session and breaks the date-time strings awkwardly ('Saturday 24 / October, 10:00 to / 13:00').
findings.impact: May make the session choice harder to scan and draws the eye to the latest session.
findings.recommendation: Order sessions chronologically and use one consistent card size per row (or a single column) so each date-time stays on one or two lines.

findings.title: Tool details table uses two different label-column widths
findings.description: Category/Deposit/Available from align values at about x=224, while Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case align at about x=180, so the values form two ragged columns in what reads as one table.
findings.impact: Small loss of polish against the 'careful' attribute; makes the spec list harder to scan.
findings.recommendation: Render the details as one list with a shared label column.

findings.title: Dark theme drops the chip background on green availability badges only
findings.description: In dark mode, 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' badges render as bare green text, while later-date badges ('Available from Sat 17 Oct', 'Wed 21 Oct', 'Sat 24 Oct') keep a grey chip. In light mode both kinds have chips. The dark theme reads as partly inverted rather than composed.
findings.impact: Dark mode is common among members; the inconsistent badge treatment may blur the available-now versus later distinction.
findings.recommendation: Give the badge-available component a dark-theme selection background that is visibly distinct from the surface.

findings.title: Short pages leave an empty band below the footer and an empty right half
findings.description: On basket and done at 1280x900 the footer ends and the lower part of the viewport is bare page ground. Confirm and done place all content in the left half of the 1088 px container, leaving the right half empty.
findings.impact: Makes the end of the flow look unfinished on desktop.
findings.recommendation: Pin the footer to the viewport bottom on short pages and decide what the wide layout does with the second column (or narrow the container).

findings.title: Masthead navigation items wrap to two lines at 375
findings.description: At 375 'Find a / tool', 'Basket / (1)' and 'Opening / times' each break across two lines, with the active underline split.
findings.impact: Looks unfinished on the main device and makes nav labels harder to read at larger text sizes.
findings.recommendation: Decide a narrow-width nav pattern that keeps each label on one line.

strengths: Copy in the desk volunteer's voice, concrete and kind: 'We text you if a tool is returned late by the previous borrower', 'Nothing is paid online.'
Calendar 'Open' tags (dots at 375) tie the date choice to the library's session mechanism.
Error summary at 375 is clear and well placed; one filled button per page is held throughout.
keep: Keep the volunteer copy and the 'Open' session markers; any added identity should come from them, not from ornament.
notes: No baseline/ folder in packet, so pairwise not run. Behaviour (focus, fades, sticky bar, search filtering) not assessable from stills. Logic issues seen in passing (Monday 12 selected as pick-up day; 'Basket (1)' after confirmation; no-results state showing full list) are left to usability evaluators. Detector output held 0 hits.
